newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich insists U.N. reform plan before U.S. pays.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich insists U.N. reform plan before U.S. pays.

text.p: U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich has told U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan that realistic reforms for the world body must come before Congress will allow payment of U.S. arrears.

In a letter released by his office on Thursday, Gingrich told Annan: "I acknowledge our treaty obligation to the U.N., but we have an equally important fiduiciary responsibility to the American taxpayer.
"It would be unconscionable to resolve the arrears issue before a real process of extensive reform is undertaken at the U.N."

Gingrich was reponding to an interview Annan had with the Washington Times which quoted him last week as saying that Congress's intention to set conditions on paying its $1 billion debt to the United Nations "is angering friends and foes alike."

President Bill Clinton has promised to pay the U.N. debt by 1999, albeit a lower amount than the U.N. says it is owed. And Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms is drafting legislation tying payments to reforms.

Referring to an administration proposal to ask for advance appropriations for arrears payments to be made later, Gingrich said that despite the administration's "unrealistic request ... the Congress will tightly link funding with reform, and one simply cannot occur without the other.

"We look forward to working with you during the course of this process as Congress seeks to come to agreement with the Clinton administration and the U.N. on a package of realistic and achievable U.N. reforms as a prerequisite to resolving the funding issue once and for all," the speaker said.
